report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is *plausible and supported by moderate evidence*, but it is too strong if interpreted as “simply adding olive oil” reliably prevents stroke for everyone. The best-supported advice is to use olive oil **in place of** butter, other saturated fats, or refined fats within an overall healthy dietary pattern.

**Evidence supporting it**
- A meta-analysis specifically examining olive oil and stroke included 38,673 participants for the stroke outcome and found an inverse association; however, much of this evidence was observational, so healthier lifestyles and diets among olive-oil users may explain part of the association.  
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24775425/
- In the French Three-City prospective study of older adults, 148 strokes occurred and higher olive-oil use was associated with lower stroke incidence after adjustment for measured dietary, lifestyle, and clinical risk factors. This supports the hypothesis but cannot establish causation.  
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21676914/
- Stronger causal evidence comes indirectly from PREDIMED: high-risk Spanish adults assigned to a **Mediterranean diet supplemented with extra-virgin olive oil** had a 33% lower stroke risk than the control group (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.46–0.98). But this tested the whole diet plus supplied oil—not olive oil alone.  
  https://www.ahajournals.org/doi/full/10.1161/strokeaha.117.017383

**Important caveats**
PREDIMED was retracted and republished because of departures from individual randomization; its reanalysis still found fewer *major cardiovascular events* in Mediterranean-diet groups, but this history reduces certainty somewhat. Also, evidence is more applicable to people at elevated cardiovascular risk and Mediterranean-style eating patterns than to all populations.  
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29897866/

Practically: choose olive oil to replace saturated-fat-rich fats, while prioritizing blood-pressure control, not smoking, exercise, and an overall Mediterranean-style diet.
